title: Rank-free stopping from a single raw trajectory
status: conditional theorem proved in note; exact finite examples checked; no external proof review or novelty audit

interface.data: One stationary raw output stream over a known finite alphabet; learner reads forward and may stop adaptively.
forbidden_or_absent: independent resets or free validation trajectories
supplied feature dictionary or row/column basis
interface.enumerated_features: All words over the alphabet through the known witness length L; no basis is supplied.

promises.spectral_gap: Known rational gamma > 0; every nonzero singular value of H_L is >= gamma.
promises.minimum_history_mass: Optional all-history coverage promise: every u in Sigma^{<=L} has probability >= p_min > 0.
promises.mixing: Known rational C_beta >= 1 and tau > 0 with beta(k) <= C_beta exp(-k/tau), under the stated block-coupling convention.
promises.confidence: delta in (0,1/4), rational for exact implementation.

result.finite_matrix: H_L[u,v]=Pr(uv), u,v in Sigma^{<=L}; rank(H_L)=rank(H)=r when L>=r-1.
result.algorithm: At look j acquire n_j=2^j fresh length-(2L+1) windows with g_j skipped symbols between windows; estimate all prefix probabilities; construct exact rational Hhat and Ghat=Hhat^T Hhat; compute positive inertia at gamma^2/16 and 9gamma^2/16; stop when both counts agree at a value d<=R, all histories were seen (if coverage requested), and the exact-comparable confidence radius E_j is < gamma/4.
result.certificate_type: Data-dependent high-probability certificate, not deterministic identification from noisy data.
result.correctness: Under the promises, returns unknown r with probability at least 1-delta. If the optional p_min coverage gate is omitted, the rank-only rule remains valid with rescaled confidence budgets.
result.stage_bounds: Let delta_j=delta/(3*2^(j+1)), k_j=ceil(log2(2M/delta_j)), h_j=ceil(log2(N/delta_j)). A sufficient look j obeys n_j > 8 N^2 gamma^(-2) k_j and, when coverage is requested, n_j >= p_min^(-1) h_j.

costs.raw_symbols: Across looks through J, fewer than 2 n_J windows and fewer than 2 n_J(B+g_J) trajectory symbols including skipped gaps.
costs.prefix_table_bits: O(M log(n_J+1)) counter bits plus a shared denominator; retained raw windows would cost O(B n_J log q) bits.
costs.linear_algebra: O(N^3) integer/rational arithmetic operations per look for Gram construction and each exact inertia computation.
costs.bit_arithmetic: Conservative schoolbook bound O(N^5(b+log N)^2) per look for exact inertia, where b=O(log N+2 log n_J+2 bitlen(gamma)); details are in RESULT.txt.
costs.model_coefficients: No realization coefficients are output; coefficient-bit cost is therefore zero. Prefix-frequency rational table is charged above. Future-prediction coefficient precision is outside the theorem.

same_data_controls.full_block_empirical_hankel_svd: Uses exactly the same windows and word counts and has the same concentration/gap sample bound. The result adds rank-free sequential stopping and exact inertia certification; it does not reduce the full matrix/table cost or claim adaptive small-basis acquisition.
same_data_controls.retained_samples: Keeping windows costs O(B n log q) bits and does not improve the statistical bound; streaming counters discard the raw windows but retain O(M log n) count bits.
same_data_controls.basis_supplied: A supplied row/column basis is a different, privileged interface; its supply/search/certification cost is not treated as free.

lower_bounds.claim: Without a uniform singular gap, no uniform finite rank-discovery sample bound holds even at fixed state cap, witness horizon, positive history mass, and geometric mixing.
lower_bounds.construction: Stationary symmetric binary Markov chain with P(1|0)=1/2-theta and P(1|1)=1/2+theta has H_1 singular values 3/2, theta, 0; distinguishing theta=0 from theta>0 costs Omega(theta^-2) symbols.

lower_bounds.claim: If the output must certify exposure of every candidate history, a prefix of mass p_min can require Omega(1/p_min) symbols to appear.
lower_bounds.construction: Binary Markov chain P(1|0)=epsilon, P(1|1)=1/2 has stationary history mass Theta(epsilon), constant geometric mixing, and all-zero path probability 1-O(T epsilon). This does not isolate p_min after fixing the Hankel gap, which also shrinks.

lower_bounds.claim: Without a state cap/witness horizon, no uniform finite word horizon identifies rank.
lower_bounds.construction: An order-m parity-dependent binary chain agrees with iid fair on every block of length <=m but has nontrivial dependence at length m+1 and predictive rank >1; its state count is 2^m. This is not used as a separate lower bound under a uniform mixing envelope.

lower_bounds.claim: Without mixing or independent restarts, a single long path may fail to reveal rank even when horizon, rank cap, gap, and minimum history mass are fixed.
lower_bounds.construction: A stationary mixture of constant-zero and constant-one paths with weights 0.9 and 0.1 has rank two and length-T TV distance 0.1 from the deterministic all-zero rank-one path for every T.

source_ledger.source: Hsu, Kakade, Zhang, A Spectral Algorithm for Learning Hidden Markov Models, COLT 2009/JCSS 2012.
source_ledger.use: Original observable-operator/spectral-learning baseline; paper explicitly uses independent sequences for its sample analysis and discusses discounting effective sample size by mixing for a long sequence. It is not the proof of this rank-free theorem.

source_ledger.source: Carlyle and Paz, Realizations by Stochastic Finite Automata, JCSS 5(1), 26-40 (1971).
source_ledger.use: Finite-rank/finite-state realization background. The finite witness length used here is derived directly.

source_ledger.source: Yu, Rates of Convergence for Empirical Processes of Stationary Mixing Sequences, Annals of Probability 22(1), 94-116 (1994).
source_ledger.use: Primary source on empirical processes under beta mixing and block/coupling methods; this note uses a direct finite-class Hoeffding bound after a standard block coupling.

source_ledger.source: Berbee, Random Walks with Stationary Increments and Renewal Theory, MC Tracts 112 (1979).
source_ledger.use: Original coupling reference. Repository metadata/full-text link were checked; the 42 MB full text could not be retrieved in this pass. The block-coupling inequality is stated with its convention and can be proved sequentially from the beta coefficient definition.

source_ledger.source: Hoeffding, Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables, JASA 58(301), 13-30 (1963).
source_ledger.use: Original source for the independent-block Bernoulli concentration inequality.

unresolved: No adaptive small-basis acquisition or subexponential-in-L method is established.
No sharp joint dependence on M, N, gamma, and p_min is established.
No coordinate-stable realization, coefficient precision, or future-horizon prediction theorem is established.
The gap, mass, and mixing envelope are assumed known; estimating them from the same path is not addressed.
No external proof review, novelty audit, or priority claim has been completed.
